trust_decision.summary: Whether an extractor-supplied (untrusted) extension may end an on-disk filename is decided by the allowlist in _UnsafeExtensionError.sanitize_extension, which _change_extension (replace_extension/prepend_extension) calls; the allowlist wrongly included the shortcut types url/desktop/webloc, which are only legitimate when yt-dlp itself writes link files.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'bypass of CVE-2024-38519' and 'insufficient filename sanitization'; the 2024 mitigation is the ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS allowlist (docstring references GHSA-79w7-vh3h-8g4j at yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:5116), and the dangerous shortcut extensions sit in its 'others' block.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `yt-dlp URL` / YoutubeDL.download -> process_info -> replace_extension on the extractor-supplied ext (fix.diff:44-54)

fix_sites.module_kind: core orchestrator (legitimate writer that must bypass the narrowed allowlist)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:3398 (_write_link_file composes prepare_filename + replace_extension; must be given an explicit per-call allowlist once url/desktop/webloc leave the global list)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 per-format route: prepend_extension is documented/tested as only checking the prepended part for slashes (test/test_utils.py:318-328), the per-format files are 'temporary' merge inputs deleted after merging, so a solver can argue they are not final output files and out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: yt-dlp's own --write-link/--write-url-link/--write-desktop-link/--write-webloc-link must keep producing .url/.desktop/.webloc files; simply deleting the three entries breaks them, and the generic extractor's direct-link fallback also reads ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS directly. The allow-unsafe-ext compat option monkeypatches sanitize_extension with a 2-arg lambda that would reject any new keyword argument.

O6_input_shapes: dotted ext where only the last component is checked (rpartition, yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:5235)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Multi-format download with a non-ffmpeg downloader names each per-format file via prepend_extension(correct_ext(temp, per-format ext), 'f<id>', per-format ext); the prepend branch only slash-checks 'f<id>' and never allowlists the per-format ext, while the merged ext (from codecs) is what existing_video_file checks.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Per-format files are temporary merge inputs and prepend_extension's slash-only behaviour is intentional and tested (test/test_utils.py:318-323).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the link-writer fix site, ~140 lines away; mechanism lives in yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:2147-2149

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a postprocessor that renames output using an info-derived ext via a path that bypasses replace_extension (plain string concatenation)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: postprocessors already rebuild filenames from info['ext'] in many places; a maintainer adding a new conversion could concatenate instead of calling the helper

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second direct-link fallback in another extractor that maps unknown exts using its own local list rather than ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS

O9_family: CWE-641 / dangerous file type creation via insufficient extension allowlisting (path/filename sanitization)

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3 + pip/hatch; pure Python, no compile step
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_utils.py:317-346 (prepend/replace_extension uncommon-extension tests); test/test_YoutubeDL.py for process_info/outtmpl

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete 'url', 'desktop', 'webloc' from ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS and stop, breaking --write-link (or add a special-case that re-allows them globally).

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix passes a new _allowed_exts kwarg to sanitize_extension, but the allow-unsafe-ext monkeypatch at yt_dlp/__init__.py:622 is `lambda x, prepend=False: x`, which would raise TypeError on every replace_extension call under that compat option (not changed by the fix).
Windows NTFS stream/trailing-dot/space filename semantics for extensions were not examined.
unverified: O8 route reachability (that an extractor can return a per-format ext like 'url' with codecs that make get_compatible_ext pick a safe merged ext, and that the per-format file survives when ffmpeg is missing or -k is set) was traced by reading only, not run.
